mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL YoY growth exceeds 2% and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by more than 0.5% in a month and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% YoY signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator for broader economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST declines by more than 10% YoY and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% MoM signals strengthening supply-side activity, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% for three consecutive months signals accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a weakening labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases simultaneously and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening consumer demand, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases and UNRATE increases simultaneously and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a shift towards restrictive policy, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month during a tightening cycle and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
